title: Fieldnote · Equipment requests
notice: Entirely fictional worked example. Answers are scripted fixtures; the prototype simulates roles and writes. No real customer material or user acceptance is implied.
outcome: A teammate can submit an equipment request, and a coordinator can decide it with a traceable reason and history.
scope: One studio; requester and coordinator roles; three equipment choices
Save draft, submit, approve, reject with reason, revise and resubmit
Visibility and self-review limits; versioned, idempotent writes; visible history
Local interactive simulation with empty, pending, invalid, error and stale states
excluded: Inventory reservations, availability guarantees, checkout and returns
Email, external integrations, real sign-in and real personal information
Production deployment and a production database schema
limits: The browser prototype uses memory only; reload and Reset clear every change. The role picker is not authentication.
Failure and latency are simulated. Server authorization, database atomicity and durable retries are specified but not implemented.
No independent builder trial, real stakeholder approval, accessibility certification or cross-platform acceptance has been completed.
This is a worked example, not a new benchmark or a change to an existing baseline.

sources.title: Initial request
sources.excerpt: Requests get lost in chat. Give teammates one place to ask for a kit and let the studio coordinator approve it.

sources.title: Discovery meeting
sources.excerpt: Maybe everyone could approve anyone's request to keep things moving.

sources.title: Clarification round 1
sources.excerpt: Only the studio coordinator; no self-approval or self-rejection.

sources.title: Clarification round 2
sources.excerpt: Other stale writes fail and tell the user to refresh; they never overwrite a decision.

questions.question: Who can see and review requests?
questions.why: The meeting suggests open approval, which conflicts with separation of duties.
questions.answer: Coordinator reviews others; requesters see only their own records; other drafts are hidden.
questions.next: Use the decision in the pilot design.

questions.question: Can a sent request be edited, and how does rejection recover?
questions.why: Editing after approval changes what was authorized.
questions.recommendation: Lock submitted requests; make rejected requests revisable.
questions.answer: Only owned drafts are editable. Rejected requests return to draft under the same ID; approvals are terminal.
questions.next: Use the decision in the pilot design.

questions.question: Does approval reserve inventory, and what is required to submit?
questions.why: No inventory feed exists; a reservation promise would be misleading.
questions.recommendation: Keep stock management outside the pilot.
questions.answer: Approval is permission only. Choose a kit, purpose and valid date range. Drafts may be incomplete.
questions.next: Use the decision in the pilot design.

questions.question: What happens on duplicate clicks or a stale review?
questions.why: Two actions must not silently overwrite each other.
questions.recommendation: Reject stale writes and replay exact retries once.
questions.answer: Use actor-scoped operation IDs, payload checks and expected versions; failed retries cannot disclose hidden records.
questions.next: Use the decision in the pilot design.

questions.question: What history remains after revision?
questions.why: A new draft must not erase why the previous submission failed.
questions.recommendation: Keep append-only events with rejection reasons.
questions.answer: Each successful operation increments version and adds an event; retries and failures do not.
questions.next: Use the decision in the pilot design.

questions.question: What does the user see during a slow or failed write?
questions.why: Optimistic status without recovery could imply an action succeeded.
questions.recommendation: Disable actions while pending; preserve data on failure.
questions.answer: Show failure and retry; never mutate the record on failed writes. Browser reload intentionally resets this simulation.
questions.next: Use the decision in the pilot design.

questions.question: Should the pilot send email?
questions.why: Recipients and delivery semantics are undefined.
questions.recommendation: Defer email and use in-app history.
questions.answer: Email is excluded from this pilot; define recipients, consent and delivery behavior before adding it.
questions.next: Define notification recipients and delivery before a later slice.

decisions.text: Coordinator reviews others; requesters see only their own records; other drafts are hidden.
Only owned drafts are editable. Rejected requests return to draft under the same ID; approvals are terminal.
Approval is permission only. Choose a kit, purpose and valid date range. Drafts may be incomplete.
Use actor-scoped operation IDs, payload checks and expected versions; failed retries cannot disclose hidden records.
Each successful operation increments version and adds an event; retries and failures do not.
Show failure and retry; never mutate the record on failed writes. Browser reload intentionally resets this simulation.
Email is excluded from this pilot; define recipients, consent and delivery behavior before adding it.

rules.text: Requesters see and mutate only their own records. Coordinator sees submitted/decided records plus own drafts; may review only others. Server identity must enforce this, including retry lookups.
Only owned Draft records allow save/submit. Coordinator may approve/reject Submitted records only. Owner may revise Rejected to Draft. Approved is terminal.
Submit requires Camera kit, Lighting kit or Audio kit; trimmed purpose length 10–240; real YYYY-MM-DD dates with end >= start. Drafts may be incomplete. Approval never reserves stock.

Each write includes expectedVersion and actor-scoped operationId. Exact same-payload retries return the previous result without another event; changed payload with the same key or a stale version fails. Check visibility first.

Rejection reason is trimmed to 5–240 characters. Every successful write increments version and appends an event. Revise clears current reason but retains history. Invalid/stale/retried writes append nothing.
Pending actions are disabled. Failure changes no record and offers retry; stale writes request an explicit refresh. Simulation uses memory and exposes no real login or persistence.
Pilot communicates decisions through status/history only; email remains excluded and Q7 deferred.

acceptance.then: the draft remains editable and one versioned event is recorded
acceptance.verify: Model + browser: save then inspect history.

acceptance.given: a draft has a short purpose or impossible/reversed date range
acceptance.then: the write fails with a field message and no state, version or history change
acceptance.verify: Model + browser: invalid dates and purpose; assert no mutation.

acceptance.when: the owner submits once then retries exactly
acceptance.then: one submitted version and event exist; retry returns the prior result
acceptance.verify: Model + browser: submit; model repeats the exact operation ID.

acceptance.given: Morgan is coordinator and a submitted request belongs to Jules
acceptance.then: the request becomes Approved; neither owner nor coordinator can edit or decide it again; no stock is reserved
acceptance.verify: Model + browser: approve, inspect terminal actions; no reservation UI.

acceptance.given: a submitted request is visible to Morgan
acceptance.when: Morgan rejects with a short reason then a valid one
acceptance.then: short reason fails without mutation; valid reason appears in current status and history
acceptance.verify: Model + browser: reject with abc, then a valid sentence.

acceptance.then: the ID stays the same, current reason clears, earlier rejection remains in history
acceptance.verify: Model + browser: complete the rejection recovery loop.

acceptance.given: an actor is a requester, another owner or a self-reviewing coordinator
acceptance.when: that actor attempts a forbidden read or transition
acceptance.then: other drafts remain hidden and the forbidden write is rejected, including replay of a cached operation
acceptance.verify: Model: direct authorization bypass attempts; browser: switch simulated roles.

acceptance.given: a decision increments the request version
acceptance.when: another write uses an old version or a reused key with a changed payload
acceptance.then: a conflict is returned and the accepted decision/history remain unchanged
acceptance.verify: Model + browser: stale-view control; model checks payload collision.

acceptance.given: a write is pending or a simulated failure occurs
acceptance.then: actions are disabled while pending; failed write preserves state; retry can succeed
acceptance.verify: Browser: enable failure simulation, submit, then Retry last action.

acceptance.given: the list is empty and then has a decided request
acceptance.then: an actionable empty state, in-app status and history are visible; no email is sent
acceptance.verify: Browser: empty-list scenario and status/history; no provider dependency.

slices.title: Authorized records and durable writes
slices.outcome: Implement authenticated identity, visibility, Request/Event/Operation storage and atomic transactions.
slices.notes: Backend first: derive actor from the session, never a supplied role. Unique(actor_id, operation_id); compare canonical payload digest; atomic version compare/update plus event+operation insert. Cache replay must enforce current visibility. Start with additive pilot tables; no legacy data migration is needed in this fictional greenfield case. Decide retention before production.

slices.title: Request and review journeys
slices.outcome: Implement form validation and the complete approval/rejection/revision loop.
slices.notes: Use shared rules and calendar-date validation on server and client. RequestEvent is append-only; keep rejection history after resubmission. Record occurred_at from server time. Index owner/status for list queries. Model is conceptual; exact SQL and identity-provider mappings remain implementation work.

slices.title: Recovery and pilot delivery
slices.outcome: Connect pending, error, stale refresh, empty state and history to a real backend.
slices.notes: Integration tests must use separate real sessions for cross-owner and self-review denial plus concurrent writes. Verify keyboard/error announcements and focus with assistive technology. Pilot behind a disabled-by-default feature flag; disable the flag to roll back, retain audit data. No email, deployment or feature enablement is authorized by this packet.
